title.narrative: MAX-D - Maximizing Due Diligence in Minerals Supply Chains

description.narrative: This project will help expand the public procurement market in Europe for responsible mining through tenders that reward supply chain actors with better human rights and environmental due diligence. It will develop local worker-driven monitoring capacity in key mining areas in Bolivia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), strengthening workers’ voices and providing evidence-based monitoring reports to inform public buyers’ engagement with their suppliers.The project combines the bottom-up approach, worker-driven monitoring, with a top-down approach, public procurement as driver for responsible sourcing and due diligence, to establish a complementary due diligence system that, after project’s end, will be financed by public buyers affiliated to Electronics Watch.In Bolivia and the DRC, it will strengthen monitoring and remediation capacity of civil society and worker organisations through trainings on methodology, supply chain due diligence, labour rights and occupational health and safety, developing complaint mechanisms, and strengthening cooperatives. It will generate risk assessments and compliance reports for artisanal and small-scale mines (ASM) and cooperative mines as well as large-scale mines (LSM), focusing on forced labour and the worst forms of child labour as well as occupational health and safety hazards and environmental degradation that undermine equitable and sustainable social and economic development.Also, the project aims to advance social dialogue with local and global supply chain actors, like mining companies, smelters, vehicle companies, and ICT hardware brands, to remediate violations and improve specific worksites, while enhancing due diligence practices. Public buyers will receive issue and due diligence guidance relating to specific cases to help drive compliance with the supply chain due diligence obligations for European Union importers under the European Union (EU) Regulation on Conflict Minerals and the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) due diligence model. As this is a new field for public buyers, the project will focus on building the capacity of the participating public buyers.
